html:
The Sixty Dome Mosque, or Shat Gombuj Masjid, stands at Bagerhat in southwestern Bangladesh and was built in the mid 15th century by Khan Jahan Ali, a Muslim commander and saint, in the time of the Bengal Sultanate.

Despite its name it has 77 small domes on a brick hall held up by sixty stone pillars. Its thick walls and curved cornices copy the bamboo huts of the Bengal village, a style typical of Bengali Islamic building. Khan Jahan cleared the forest at the edge of the Sundarbans, dug tanks for water and built a whole town of mosques, roads and bridges, called Khalifatabad.

He is still honoured as a saint, and his tomb, guarded by crocodiles in its pond, draws pilgrims. Along with the spread of Sufi preachers, settlers like him helped make the eastern delta mostly Muslim. The mosque city has been a World Heritage Site since 1985.
